rows: A temporary {opportunity} grants access to {location} or {target} that is normally unreachable.
The opening is real, but the window for using it is short or uncertain.
What becomes possible if the access is used, shared or ignored?
Someone else learns about the opening before it closes.
Who would object to its use?
Something Valuable Has No Clear Owner
A valuable {resource} becomes available with no uncontested owner or authority.
Multiple actors discover the opportunity at nearly the same time.
What changes depending on who claims or protects the resource?
A message offers access to an {opportunity} that seems tailored to the recipients.
The sender knows something they should not obviously know.
What is gained by accepting, investigating or refusing?
The same invitation reaches a rival.
Why these recipients and why now?
A Breakthrough Needs a Field Test
An {initiating_actor} has a new method, device or discovery that could change access to a {resource} or problem.
The breakthrough works in controlled conditions but needs a real-world test.
Who benefits or loses if the breakthrough succeeds?
A limitation appears only under pressure.
What assumptions have not been tested?
Who wants the result suppressed or accelerated?
The Map Shows More Than a Place
A newly found {evidence} points toward {location}, but also implies something unexpected about its significance.
Another interpretation of the map or record points somewhere else.
What becomes possible by reaching or understanding the place?
A rival obtains a partial copy.
What part is symbolic, outdated or deliberately obscured?
A valued role, office, route or privilege becomes available after an unexpected vacancy.
Selection must happen before the usual process can settle everyone’s concerns.
Who gains influence depending on who fills the vacancy?
A previously ineligible candidate becomes viable.
A change creates sudden demand for a {resource}, service or expertise the characters can access.
Prices, alliances or social expectations shift before supply catches up.
Who is helped or harmed by meeting the demand?
A rival begins controlling a key bottleneck.
What second-order effects follow from supplying it?
An Enemy of the Problem Offers Help
An {initiating_actor} with reasons not to be trusted offers useful help against a shared {threat}.
The offer is specific enough to be credible and limited enough to avoid easy certainty.
What changes if cooperation succeeds or becomes public?
The ally asks for a concession unrelated to the immediate threat.
A piece of old {evidence} becomes newly interpretable because of a recent change or discovery.
The interpretation suggests an opportunity that earlier readers could not act on.
What can now be restored, reached, prevented or understood?
A competing interpretation implies a dangerous alternative.
Why was the knowledge unusable before?
Who else can interpret it now?
A {location} can provide shelter, access or recovery that the characters currently lack.
The haven is genuine, but accepting it creates a new relationship or expectation.
What obligation, visibility or dependency comes with shelter?
The haven becomes contested or politically visible.
What would cause the offer to end?
A {threat} becomes credible and a {deadline} makes delay materially costly.
The first consequence arrives sooner than expected.
What is lost at each stage of delay?
The deadline moves forward or gains a second condition.
Can the pressure be reduced, redirected or bought off?
An {authority_actor} or force intends to remove {affected_actor} from {location}.
The removal date is announced or enforcement begins.
What is lost beyond physical possession of the place?
A legal, political or practical exception becomes possible but contested.
A harmful {disruption} begins spreading among people, places or systems.
A new case appears outside the assumed boundary.
What must be protected before spread reaches it?
Containment itself creates a new social or resource crisis.
Something Is Hunting by a Pattern
A {threat} is targeting people or assets according to a pattern that is only partly understood.
The next likely target can be identified, but not with certainty.
What happens if the pattern is misunderstood?
The threat changes its pattern after being noticed.
Is the pattern preference, constraint or bait?
A hostile force or unavoidable event will reach {location} after a known or estimated {deadline}.
People must decide what to defend, move, hide or abandon before arrival.
What cannot all be saved at once?
The threat arrives through an unexpected route or with unexpected demands.
Can the threat be delayed or diverted?
An {initiating_actor} threatens to reveal or exploit {evidence} unless an {obligation} is met.
The threat is credible, but the blackmailer’s control over the information may be incomplete.
What is damaged by disclosure, compliance or counterpressure?
A second party learns part of the secret independently.
How much does the blackmailer actually know?
Available {resource} will not cover all expected needs before the next resupply or recovery window.
The shortage becomes visible to people who disagree about allocation.
Who bears risk under each allocation choice?
A hidden cache or alternative source appears with strings attached.
Is scarcity real, manipulated or unevenly distributed?
A fragile agreement between opposed actors will end at {deadline} unless something changes.
A provocation makes each side doubt the other’s willingness to continue.
What resumes if the truce fails?
Evidence emerges that a third actor benefits from collapse.
What minimum does each side need to continue?
A machine, structure or process tied to {resource} is operating beyond safe limits.
Indicators show a {deadline} before failure, but estimates disagree.
What depends on continued operation and what is endangered by it?
An attempted stabilization reveals a hidden dependency.
Was the overload accidental, necessary or deliberate?
An {authority_actor} will make a decision at {deadline} that changes access, law, status or resources.
Interested groups begin accelerating pressure before ordinary deliberation can finish.
Who gains or loses if the decision stands?
New evidence appears too late for normal procedure.
Who can still influence the decision?
What happens if procedure is disrupted?
